Comparative efficacy of glucose-lowering medications on body weight and blood pressure in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis

One-page synthesis

The supplement documents a very large network meta-analysis of glucose-lowering therapies for body weight, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure in type 2 diabetes. The update flow adds 18 new trials to 406 trials from an earlier review, yielding 424 trials. The appendix supplies reproducible search strategies, study/baseline characteristics, heterogeneity and inconsistency diagnostics, outcome-specific risk-of-bias assessments, funnel plots, pairwise meta-analysis, network league tables, CINeMA confidence assessments, and prespecified subgroup/sensitivity analyses.

At the drug-class level versus placebo, the clearest body-weight reductions were observed with GLP-1 receptor agonists (MD -1.98, 95% CI -2.23 to -1.73) and SGLT-2 inhibitors (-1.85, -2.13 to -1.58), with a smaller reduction for metformin (-0.64, -1.02 to -0.26). For systolic blood pressure, SGLT-2 inhibitors (-2.89, -3.37 to -2.40) and GLP-1 receptor agonists (-2.33, -2.86 to -1.80) showed the largest class-level reductions among the plotted drug classes. For diastolic blood pressure, SGLT-2 inhibitors (-1.44, -1.68 to -1.20) and pioglitazone (-1.04, -1.58 to -0.49) were significant versus placebo. These are review-level network estimates, not individual-patient predictions.

Methods and evidence quality

Heterogeneity and inconsistency

Supplement 4 reports estimated heterogeneity values of 1.1203 for body weight, 1.8278 for systolic BP, and 0.1639 for diastolic BP. Supplement 5 identifies statistically detectable global inconsistency for body weight (8/94 inconsistent comparisons; 8.51%; design-by-treatment Q=150.68, df=111, p=0.01), whereas the corresponding global tests for systolic BP (p=0.94) and diastolic BP (p=0.93) do not indicate inconsistency.

Risk of bias, reporting bias, and confidence

The supplement provides outcome-specific risk-of-bias tables across many included trials, comparison-adjusted funnel plots for all three outcomes, and CINeMA comparison-level confidence tables. Confidence is not uniform: for body weight, for example, canagliflozin-placebo and dapagliflozin-placebo are rated high, empagliflozin-placebo and ertugliflozin-placebo moderate, oral semaglutide-placebo moderate, and subcutaneous semaglutide-placebo high. This heterogeneity in certainty is important when interpreting rankings.

Subgroup and sensitivity analyses

Separate league tables are provided for body weight, systolic BP, and diastolic BP by trial duration/background treatment and, for body weight, baseline BMI, plus sensitivity analyses restricted to low-risk-of-bias trials and analyses excluding trials with imputed missing standard deviations. These analyses strengthen auditability, but the supplement-focused appraisal does not collapse every matrix cell into a single ranking.

Evaluation and appraisal

Verdict: Read soon. This is a methodologically rich and highly reusable 2021 evidence map for weight and BP effects of glucose-lowering therapies. Use it as historical/comparative evidence, not as a stand-alone current prescribing authority.

Relevance: 8/10

Directly useful for comparing weight and blood-pressure effects across major glucose-lowering classes.

Evidence basis: Large RCT network and detailed supplement.

Limiting factor: Search ends in 2020 and does not represent newer agents/evidence.

Would raise/lower: A current update using newer trials and agents.

Novelty: 7/10

The network comparison integrates many drug classes and three cardiometabolic outcomes.

Evidence basis: 424-trial evidence network and class/drug league tables.

Limiting factor: The source is from 2021 and the question has since evolved.

Would raise/lower: A contemporary update with newer agents and head-to-head evidence.

Method strength: 8/10

The package documents reproducible searches, network analyses, heterogeneity/inconsistency assessment, risk of bias, sensitivity/subgroup analyses, and CINeMA.

Evidence basis: Supplements 1-20 plus PRISMA-NMA checklist.

Limiting factor: Main article full text was absent from the selected folder, limiting full narrative-method verification.

Would raise/lower: Direct review of the complete article plus protocol and analytic code/data.

Evidence strength: 7/10

The network is very large and uncertainty is reported, but body-weight inconsistency is statistically detectable and certainty varies by comparison.

Evidence basis: 424 trials; Supplement 5; CINeMA tables.

Limiting factor: Network estimates depend on transitivity/indirect evidence and comparison-level confidence varies.

Would raise/lower: More direct head-to-head trials and a newer network with robust consistency.

External validity: 8/10

The network spans many glucose-lowering classes and trials, supporting broad T2D applicability.

Evidence basis: Wide treatment network and 422 cited trials/reports.

Limiting factor: Trial populations and background therapies vary; individual patient applicability is not established by class averages.

Would raise/lower: Patient-level meta-analysis or prespecified effect-modifier analysis.

Implementation value: 7/10

The class-vs-placebo magnitudes are useful for treatment tradeoff discussions but should not determine current prescribing alone.

Evidence basis: Body-weight and BP league tables with sensitivity/subgroup analyses.

Limiting factor: No glycemic, cardiovascular, renal, safety, cost, or current-guideline synthesis in this supplement-focused appraisal.

Would raise/lower: Integration with current outcomes, safety, comorbidity, and guideline evidence.

Main strengths

  • Large evidence network with explicit trial flow and extensive supporting tables.
  • Transparent network diagnostics, risk-of-bias tables, funnel plots, CINeMA, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses.
  • Clinically interpretable weight and BP outcomes with class- and drug-level comparisons.

Main limitations

  • Evidence search and network are dated relative to 2026 practice; the source cannot represent subsequent trials, drugs, doses, or outcome evidence.
  • Body-weight network shows statistically detectable inconsistency.
  • Network estimates combine direct and indirect evidence and rely on transitivity assumptions.
  • The selected Drive packet lacks the main article full text, constraining appraisal of narrative methods, author interpretation, limitations, funding role, and full discussion.
  • This review does not by itself integrate glycemic efficacy, cardiovascular/renal outcomes, adverse effects, contraindications, cost, or patient preferences.

Implementation / practice takeaways

Best use
Historical comparative evidence for expected class-level effects on weight and BP in type 2 diabetes, and a source map for identifying underlying RCTs.
Do not use for
Current drug selection in isolation or patient-specific effect prediction.
High-value signal
GLP-1 RAs and SGLT-2 inhibitors show concurrent class-level reductions in weight and systolic BP versus placebo in this network.
Interpretation caution
Class rankings should be read alongside comparison-level CINeMA confidence and the body-weight inconsistency signal.
